title: PK Document Tracking System — Process Flow

pages.title: Sign in and find documents
pages.summary: Sign in, find the document you need and use the actions available to your account.

steps.text: Sign in with the account supplied by the account administrator.
If asked, choose a new password before opening the workspace.
Open Overview, Hardcopy Documents, Softcopy Documents or External Documents.
Use folders, Search and filters; choose View Details to read the full record.
Show records and actions allowed by the staff member's account permissions.
Choose Download or Print when available for the current file; External Documents offer Download.

notes: Document visibility, editing, approval and file use depend on separate permissions.
Hardcopy records track physical documents. Softcopy and External Documents can include controlled files.

pages.title: Register or edit a hardcopy
pages.summary: An authorized holder records a physical document. Saving applies the change immediately.

steps.text: Open Hardcopy Documents and choose Add New Hardcopy Document, or Edit an active record.
Enter Document Title and choose Area, Specific, optional Asset and Location.
Check Current Holder and retention dates; add optional Reason / Notes for a new document.
Choose Save Document and confirm the change.
Validate storage, holder and dates; save the active record and its history.

notes: Only the current holder with direct hardcopy permission, or an Administrator, can edit an active hardcopy.
Administrators may select another active holder. Other users register themselves as holder.
Register and edit hardcopies directly. New Hardcopy Create and Update requests are unavailable.

pages.title: Monitor hardcopy storage and retention
pages.summary: Check the storage place and retention dates, then arrange any required follow-up.

steps.text: Open Hardcopy Documents; use folders or Search to find the document.
Open View Details and check its Area, Specific, Asset, Location and Current Holder.
When editing, enable Track retention period and enter Retention Start and Retention End.
Show the days remaining, Due today or an overdue message using office dates.
Use Due Today, Overdue, Due in the Next 7 Days or Due in 8-30 Days to review records.
Review the physical document, then arrange a permitted update, transfer or disposal.

notes: Both retention dates are required when tracking is enabled. Retention End must be on or after Retention Start.
Reminders cover visible active hardcopies whose retention end date has arrived. Retention never triggers automatic disposal.
Several hardcopy documents may share one Location. The displayed Location sequence belongs to that storage place.

pages.title: Create or revise a softcopy directly
pages.summary: An authorized controller creates a softcopy or publishes a revision without an approval request.

steps.text: Open Softcopy Documents; choose Add New Softcopy Document, or Edit an active record.
Choose Create Softcopy or Revise Softcopy; enter Subject / Reason and Proposed Document Title.
For creation, choose Category; for revision, choose Existing Softcopy Document.
Check Number of Pages; attach Document File and enter optional Effective Date and Remarks.
Choose Approve Directly and confirm.
Create the active document or publish its next revision with the replacement file.

notes: The system generates a new document number. Need Series Number? allows an existing category number with a unique series.
A file is required: PDF, TXT, PNG, JPG/JPEG, DOCX or XLSX, up to 15 MB. A blank direct Effective Date uses the approval date.
Revision keeps the document number, series and category. Softcopy cancellation is unavailable; authorized disposal is separate.

pages.title: Create or revise an external document directly
pages.summary: An authorized controller records a document from outside the company and publishes its current file.

steps.text: Open External Documents; choose Add New External Document, or Edit an active record.
Enter Document Title, choose Category and add an optional Description.
Choose Attach File. A revision also requires a replacement file.
Choose Save Directly and confirm.
Create an active record at revision 00, or publish the next revision and its replacement file.

notes: External Documents use External Categories and do not use retention dates.
Attach PDF, TXT, PNG, JPG/JPEG, DOCX or XLSX, up to 15 MB. Description may contain up to 2,000 characters.
Revising a record or using its file requires the appropriate permission and document access.

pages.title: Request a new document or revision
pages.summary: Submit a proposed softcopy or external document change. Final approval applies it to the live register.

steps.text: Open My Requests; choose Softcopy Request or External Document Request, then New Request.
Choose Create or Revise for the document type; enter Subject / Reason.
For a revision, select the existing document; enter the proposed title and other displayed details.
For creation, choose its category; attach the required file and add optional Remarks.
Choose Save Draft and confirm. Review the draft, then choose Submit and confirm.
Follow the published approval route; create the document or publish the revision after final approval.

notes: Softcopy creation also asks for Number of Pages and supports optional series. Its number and revision are assigned when approved.
External requests use External Create Request or External Revised Request. Enter Description and upload the required Attach File.
Uploads accept PDF, TXT, PNG, JPG/JPEG, DOCX or XLSX, up to 15 MB. A pending attachment is not the current approved file.

pages.title: Save, submit or remove your draft
pages.summary: Save a proposal, review it and submit it for approval. An unsubmitted draft can be cancelled.

steps.text: Open the relevant My Requests tab, choose New Request and complete the form.
Choose Save Draft and confirm; use Edit to correct your Draft or Returned request.
Open View Details, check the proposal and use Review File when available.
Choose Submit and confirm when the request is ready for approval.
Validate permissions, active choices and files; mark Submitted and notify the first approver.

notes: Only the requester can edit their Draft or Returned request. Submitted requests keep the route recorded at submission.
An existing Submitted Access, Assignment or Transfer request blocks another of these for the same requester and document.
Only the requester can Cancel a Draft. Delete permanently removes an eligible Cancelled draft only if it was never submitted.

pages.title: Review, approve, return or reject
pages.summary: Assigned approvers decide in order. Final approval applies the change or prepares a physical transfer.

steps.text: Open My Tasks; select the request and review View Details and the Approval Process Timeline.
Use Review File when available; check the proposal, attachments and earlier decisions.
Choose one decision: Approve, Return or Reject. Add optional remarks and confirm.
Record the decision and history; update the status and route work to the responsible person.
Open the updated request; check its status, remarks and next required action.

notes: Approve advances the route. Final approval usually marks Completed; a transfer stays Approved until Dispatch and Accept finish.
Later Return reopens the previous approver and stays Submitted. First-step Return marks Returned; requester edits and resubmits on the original route.
Reject marks Rejected and ends the route. Only the assigned user or matching role member can decide; Administrator status gives no bypass.

pages.title: Request and approve a hardcopy transfer
pages.summary: Approve the receiving user and destination before the physical document is released.

steps.text: Open My Requests > Hardcopy Transfer Request and choose New Request.
Choose Hardcopy Document; check Original Places and Holder from its current record.
Choose Destination Area, Specific, optional Asset and a different Location.
Choose Receiving User; enter Request Subject and optional Remarks, then Save Draft and Submit.
Review and approve the proposed transfer through the request's approval route.
Create a For Transfer handoff; retain the current holder and storage place until acceptance.

notes: Source and destination choices must be active and allowed. The destination needs Area, Specific and Location; Asset is optional.
The requester may differ from the Current Holder. Only the original requester can later choose Dispatch.
Default route: Plant Manager, Document Control Officer, then Requester confirmation. Check the published route for changes.

pages.title: Dispatch and accept the physical document
pages.summary: The original requester dispatches the approved hardcopy. The named recipient accepts it after physical receipt.

steps.text: Open My Tasks > Hardcopy Transfer Request and find Physical Transfer Handoffs.
For a For Transfer handoff, release the document, choose Dispatch and confirm.
Mark the handoff In Transit and record who dispatched it and when.
After physical receipt, open Physical Transfer Handoffs, choose Accept and confirm.
Check the active document and Location, unchanged holder and approved storage path.
Set the recipient as holder, update the storage place, mark Accepted and complete the request.

notes: Only the original requester can Dispatch. Only the named receiving user can Accept an In Transit handoff.
A changed holder, unavailable Location or changed approved storage path blocks acceptance and leaves the handoff unchanged.
When the holder changes, acceptance revokes the previous holder's personal hardcopy access grants. Global permissions still apply.

pages.title: Request temporary document access
pages.summary: Request access to a softcopy or hardcopy until a chosen expiry date. Holder and assignments stay unchanged.

steps.text: Open My Requests > Document Access Request and choose New Request.
Choose Softcopy or Hardcopy and its document; check your name under Recipient / Assigned User.
Enter Subject / Reason, set Access Expires At after today and add optional Remarks.
Choose Save Draft, then Submit; confirm each action.
Review the access request and complete its approval route.
Grant access through the approved expiry date; retain the current holder and assignments.

notes: This request is for you. Recipient / Assigned User cannot be changed to another person.
Expiry must still be valid at final approval. Access ends at the end of the selected date, or earlier if revoked.
The account's document and file permissions still apply. Catalog visibility alone does not grant download, print or edit rights.

pages.title: Request a document assignment
pages.summary: Ask to become a softcopy assignee or the recorded holder of an active hardcopy.

steps.text: Open My Requests > Document Assignment Request and choose New Request.
Choose Softcopy or Hardcopy and its document; check your name under Recipient / Assigned User.
Enter Subject / Reason and optional Remarks; choose Save Draft, then Submit and confirm.
Review the proposed assignment and complete the request's approval route.
For a softcopy, add the requester as an assignee while keeping existing assignees.
For a hardcopy, set the requester as Current Holder; retain its storage place.

notes: This request is for the requester. An authorized document controller uses Document Assignments to assign another person.
Hardcopy assignment changes the recorded holder after final approval. It does not move the document or use Dispatch and Accept.
Assignment does not create a temporary access grant. The account's document and file permissions still apply.

pages.title: Assign one document directly
pages.summary: An authorized controller assigns a softcopy or changes the recorded holder of a hardcopy immediately.

steps.text: Open Document Assignments; choose Hardcopy / Places or Softcopy / Categories.
Choose Assign Document; select the active document and Assigned User.
Choose Save Assignment and confirm.
Validate the active document and user; check for an active hardcopy handoff.
Change the hardcopy holder or add the softcopy assignee; retain the storage place.

notes: Direct assignment requires its own permission and takes effect immediately. It needs no approval, Dispatch or Accept.
Hardcopy assignment changes the recorded holder and keeps the storage place. It does not physically move the document.
Softcopy assignment keeps existing assignees. An active Hardcopy transfer blocks reassignment. File permissions still apply.

pages.title: Assign all hardcopies at a Location
pages.summary: An authorized controller changes the recorded holder of every active hardcopy at one Location.

steps.text: Open Document Assignments and choose Hardcopy / Places.
Choose Location and Assigned User; review the active records at that Location.
Choose Assign All and confirm.
Validate the user and active records, the 2,000-document limit and any active handoffs.
Change the holder for the whole selection; keep each document at its recorded storage place.

notes: Bulk assignment includes all active hardcopies at the selected Location, up to 2,000 documents.
For Transfer or In Transit handoffs block hardcopy reassignment. Resolve the active transfer before retrying.
Direct assignment needs its own permission and no approval, Dispatch or Accept. It changes records without physically moving documents.

pages.title: Assign a softcopy category branch
pages.summary: An authorized controller assigns a user to every active softcopy in a category and its subcategories.

steps.text: Open Document Assignments and choose Softcopy / Categories.
Choose Category / Subcategory and Assigned User; review the selected category branch.
Choose Assign All and confirm.
Validate the active user, selected records and 2,000-document bulk limit.
Add the user as an assignee for the whole selection; keep existing assignees.

notes: The selected category and all its subcategories are included. Only active softcopies are assigned, up to 2,000 documents.
Direct assignment requires its own permission and takes effect immediately, without an approval request.
Assignment does not create a temporary personal access grant. The account's document and file permissions still apply.

pages.title: Dispose of a document directly
pages.summary: An authorized holder or controller records the disposal method and applies disposal immediately.

steps.text: Open the permitted document register and choose Dispose on an active record.
Choose Shred, Scratch or Other; describe the method when choosing Other.
Confirm the direct disposal.
Check both direct permissions, the disposal reason and document eligibility.
Mark Disposed and record the method, responsible person and disposal history.

notes: Direct disposal supports all three registers and needs both direct permissions. Other requires a description of up to 250 characters.
Direct Hardcopy disposal retains Location and personal grants. Softcopy disposal retires its controlled files.
External disposal keeps stored files and revision records but blocks normal download. Retention never triggers automatic disposal.

pages.title: Request hardcopy or external disposal
pages.summary: Submit a proposed disposal for approval. The document changes only after final approval.

steps.text: Open My Requests > Disposal Request and choose New Request.
Choose Hardcopy or External and its active document; complete the displayed request details.
Choose Shred, Scratch or Other; describe Other and add optional Remarks.
Choose Save Draft, review the proposal, then Submit; confirm each action.
Review the proposal and decide through the request's approval route.
After final approval, mark Disposed and retain the approval and disposal history.

notes: Disposal requests support Hardcopy and External Documents only. Softcopy disposal is available as a permitted direct action.
Other requires a description of up to 250 characters. A Return or Reject leaves the proposed disposal unapplied.
Approved Hardcopy disposal clears Location and personal grants. External disposal keeps stored files and revision records.

pages.title: Maintain places and document categories
pages.summary: Prepare the active storage places and category folders used in document forms.

steps.text: Open Setup Places and choose Area, Specific, Asset Number, Location, Softcopy Category or External Category.
Create Area, link Specific to Area, then add optional Asset Numbers under Specific.
For Location, enter Location Name, Area and Specific; add optional Asset Number and Archive Date.
For a category, enter its name and folder name; select an optional parent and softcopy code pattern.
Save and confirm; use Edit or Deactivate when permitted.
Validate parents, category nesting and unique sequence or code rules; update the available choices.

notes: A Location can omit Asset Number. Its Sequence is unique within its Specific and is assigned automatically when left empty.
Softcopy Categories and External Categories are separate. Only softcopy categories define a document numbering pattern.
Deactivation removes a choice from active selection; it does not delete the existing document records.

pages.title: Manage users, roles and permissions
pages.summary: Create staff accounts, assign roles and control which pages and actions each user can access.

steps.text: Open Roles & Permissions; choose Add Role or Edit, select its allowed actions, then Save Role.
Open User Management; choose Add User or Edit and enter the staff member's account details.
Choose Primary role, Assigned roles and an optional Leader; check Active account and choose Save User.
Give temporary credentials to the intended staff member; reset the temporary password when needed.
Sign in with the temporary password and complete the required password change.
Review Assigned Documents; deactivate a user or unused role, or Remove an eligible role.

notes: Active roles combine a user's permissions. The Leader receives approval steps configured as Requester's leader.
A delegated administrator cannot grant permissions they do not hold or create an Administrator role assignment.
Roles still used by accounts or approval routes cannot be removed. Account and role actions each require their own permission.

pages.title: Publish an approval route
pages.summary: Set the ordered approval steps for future submissions. Existing requests keep their recorded route.

steps.text: Open Workflow Builder and select the request type and its version.
Choose Start First Draft or Create Next Draft.
Choose Add Approval Step; name the step and select a role, person, requester's leader or requester.
Choose Save Step; edit, reorder or Remove steps to match the business process.
Choose Validate & Publish and confirm.
Publish the valid route for future submissions; retain the route already recorded by existing requests.

notes: Published versions are read-only. Create a draft to change future approvals.
Submission must resolve active approvers. A route that needs a requester's leader cannot start without an active assigned leader.
Check the published route for the actual approval order. Default route examples may change.

pages.title: Follow notices and review the audit trail
pages.summary: Use notices to find work needing attention. Authorized auditors can trace recorded system actions.

steps.text: Check the counts beside My Requests and My Tasks and open the relevant tab.
Highlight the user's Draft or Returned requests, assigned approvals and physical handoff tasks.
Open a task reminder and review the request before taking its permitted action.
Open a retention reminder and review the hardcopy's due or overdue date.
Open Internal Audit Trail; use Search and filters to locate the recorded actions.
Open View Details to check who acted, when the action occurred and the recorded outcome.

notes: Approval Process Timeline and request history explain request decisions. Internal Audit Trail records wider system actions.
Reminders do not approve, dispatch, accept or dispose of documents; the responsible person still confirms the action.
Counts and alerts reflect the signed-in account's allowed work. Dates and times use Asia/Manila.

pages.title: Create, download and import a backup
pages.summary: Create protected recovery copies, download or import an archive, and clean up eligible older files.

steps.text: Open Backup & Restore and check that backup setup is ready.
Choose Backup now and confirm to create an encrypted recovery archive.
Create and list the completed archive; show its type, creation time and size.
Choose Download and store the backup in a secure location.
To add an existing archive, choose Import backup, select Backup ZIP and confirm.
Choose Clean up when appropriate; confirm removal of eligible archives older than three months.

notes: A backup contains system records, application code and private files. Routine temporary files and existing backup archives are excluded.
The daily backup target is 5:00 PM, Asia/Manila. Automatic runs require the server scheduler to be configured and verified.
Import verifies and stores a backup; it does not restore live data. Clean up applies to eligible backup, audit and log archives.

pages.title: Restore system data from a backup
pages.summary: Replace live records and private files with a verified backup, then sign in and check the restored system.

steps.text: Open Backup & Restore and choose Restore system data.
Choose Backup to restore; enter Your password and type RESTORE to confirm.
Choose Restore selected backup and confirm replacement of the live records and private files.
Validate the archive and authorization; create a recovery backup before replacing live data.
Pause normal use, restore records and private files, then sign out the restoring operator.
Sign in again and check the restored records, attachments and normal business actions.

notes: Plan a maintenance period: restoration replaces current records and private files with the selected backup's contents.
Enter the operator's account password. The server must also be configured to open and verify the protected archive.
The web restore does not replace application code. A system maintainer handles code recovery separately when needed.
